title: Has It All Been Solved? Open NLP Research Questions Not Solved by Large Language Models
extended_summary:
This paper is a position-style overview that argues the rapid progress of large language models (LLMs) has not solved the full research agenda in NLP. The authors ask what research questions remain open despite LLM capabilities and compile a set of research directions that are not directly solvable by LLMs. The paper is motivated by concerns that public discourse and funding priorities are collapsing NLP into LLM development, potentially obscuring many other important areas.

The paper does not study an intervention or conduct an empirical evaluation. Instead, it presents a structured taxonomy of 14 research areas spanning fundamental, responsible, and applied NLP. These include multilinguality, reasoning, knowledge bases, language grounding, child language acquisition, non-verbal communication, ethics, interpretability, efficient NLP, NLP in online environments, healthcare, education, computational social science, and synthetic datasets. Within each area, the authors outline open problems and cite representative prior work.

The paper’s education-related discussion is especially relevant to concerns about reliability, misinformation, and overreliance: it notes that intelligent tutoring systems and educational explanation generation require human-in-the-loop checks, because LLMs still struggle with reasoning and grounding, can produce convincingly written but unverified output, and may encourage overreliance if used as a replacement for human teachers. More broadly, the paper emphasizes that LLMs can be unreliable due to hallucinations and factual inconsistencies, so they should be treated as tools to support—not replace—human expertise.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a perspective/overview paper that enumerates open research questions in NLP and LLMs rather than evaluating an educational technology intervention. It does not report an empirical design, sample, or outcome analysis relevant to K-12 evidence standards.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper provides no measured educational impact, effect sizes, or implementation results for science inquiry supports in K-12. Its relevance to the requested topic is conceptual only, mainly noting that LLMs still struggle with reasoning, grounding, hallucination, and reliability.
